title: Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship 2027: Win a $20,000 College Scholarship for Outstanding High School Seniors in the United States
summary: The Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship 2027 is now accepting applications from eligible high school seniors across the United States. Recognized as one of the country s most prestigious merit-based scholarship programs, the Coca-Cola Scholars Program rewards exceptional students who have demonstrated outstanding leadership, academic excellence, and a strong commitment to serving their schools and communities. Administered by the Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation , the program awards 150 scholarships worth $20,000 each every year to graduating high school seniors who have made meaningful contributions through leadership and community service. Since its establishment in 1986 , the Foundation has invested more than $90 million in scholarships and supported over 7,200 Coca-Cola Scholars , making it one of the nation s most respected scholarship initiatives. If you are a high-achieving student planning to pursue higher education in the United States, this scholarship presents an outstanding opportunity to receive financial support while joining a nationwide network of influential student leaders. About the Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship The Coca-Cola Scholars Program is an achievement-based scholarship , meaning recipients are selected based on their accomplishments rather than their financial need. Unlike many scholarship programs, applicants are evaluated on several qualities, including: Academic excellence Leadership potential Community service Positive impact on school and community Commitment to creating meaningful change The Foundation looks for students who have consistently demonstrated the ability to lead others, contribute to society, and excel academically throughout high school. Each year: 150 students are selected as Coca-Cola Scholars. Each recipient receives a $20,000 college scholarship . Scholars become part of an extensive alumni network of leaders making a difference across various professions and communities. Scholarship Value Successful applicants will receive: A $20,000 scholarship to support college education. Membership in the prestigious Coca-Cola Scholars alumni network. Leadership development opportunities. National recognition as a Coca-Cola Scholar. Opportunities to connect with fellow scholars and leaders from across the United States. Who Can Apply? To be eligible for the 2027 Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship, applicants must meet all of the following requirements: Educational Requirements Applicants must: Be currently enrolled as a high school or home-schooled student. Attend school in: One of the 50 U.S. states The District of Columbia Puerto Rico Or an eligible Department of Defense (DoD) school abroad. Graduate during the 2026–2027 academic school year . Plan to pursue a degree at an accredited U.S. post-secondary institution. Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (B average) . Citizenship Requirements Applicants must be one of the following: U.S. Citizen U.S. National U.S. Permanent Resident Refugee Asylee Cuban-Haitian Entrant Humanitarian Parolee Applicants must meet these citizenship requirements at the time of application and no later than Wednesday, September 30, 2026 . A pending immigration application does not establish eligibility. Who Is Not Eligible? The following individuals are not eligible for the scholarship: International students (except students attending eligible Department of Defense schools abroad). Students attending American or expatriate schools outside the eligible geographic areas. High school graduates. Students who took a gap year or are non-traditional students. Temporary residents. Students graduating from: Guam U.S. Virgin Islands Northern Mariana Islands American Samoa American or expatriate schools abroad Children or grandchildren of current Coca-Cola employees, officers, owners, or certain retired employees receiving Coca-Cola retirement benefits. Is the Scholarship Based on Financial Need? No. The Coca-Cola Scholars Program is not a need-based or income-based scholarship . Instead, selection is based on: Leadership Academic achievement Service to school and community Financial need is not used as a selection criterion. Coca-Cola Scholars Selection Process The scholarship selection process consists of four competitive phases . Phase 1: Online Application The initial online application opens annually between August 3 and September 30 . During this stage: No essays are required. No transcript is required. No recommendation letters are required. Students simply complete the online application before the deadline. Phase 2: Semifinalists By the end of October: Applicants receive notification of their application status. Approximately 1% of applicants advance as Semifinalists. Semifinalists must submit: Essays Official transcript Recommendation letter Phase 3: Regional Finalists Around 250 Regional Finalists are selected from approximately 1,200 Semifinalists . These finalists participate in interviews conducted by Coca-Cola Scholar alumni and Foundation staff during late January or early February. Phase 4: Coca-Cola Scholars Following the interview process: 150 students are officially selected as Coca-Cola Scholars. Selected students attend the required Coke Scholars Weekend in Atlanta to confirm their selection. Application Period Applications for the 2027 Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship are open: Opening Date: Monday, August 3, 2026 Closing Date: Wednesday, September 30, 2026 Deadline Time: 5:00 PM Eastern Time Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications well before the closing deadline to avoid technical issues or last-minute complications. APPLY NOW Why This Scholarship Stands Out The Coca-Cola Scholars Program has become one of America s most respected scholarship initiatives because it recognizes students who have already demonstrated exceptional leadership and service before entering college. Recipients not only receive substantial financial assistance but also gain access to a lifelong community of scholars, networking opportunities, leadership experiences, and national recognition. For ambitious high school seniors who aspire to create positive change in their communities, becoming a Coca-Cola Scholar represents both a significant honor and an investment in their future. Application Tips To improve your chances of success: Apply well before the September 30 deadline. Ensure your academic records reflect a minimum 3.0 GPA. Highlight meaningful leadership roles. Showcase community service activities with measurable impact. Prepare early in case you advance to the semifinalist stage, where essays, transcripts, and recommendation letters become required. Verify that you meet all citizenship and school eligibility requirements before applying. See FAQs here. Conclusion The 2027 Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship offers an exceptional opportunity for outstanding U.S. high school seniors to receive a $20,000 scholarship while joining one of the nation s most prestigious leadership communities. Rather than focusing on financial need, the Foundation seeks students who have demonstrated academic excellence, leadership, and a lasting commitment to serving others. Eligible students should take advantage of this opportunity by preparing their application early and ensuring they meet every eligibility requirement before the application deadline of 5:00 PM Eastern Time on Wednesday, September 30, 2026 . With only 150 scholarships awarded annually , the selection process is highly competitive, making early preparation and a strong application essential. Visit the OFY website for more Scholarship Opportunities . title: Amnesty International Free Online Human Rights Courses: Learn in 30+ Languages and Earn Certificates
summary: Amnesty International is offering free online courses through its Human Rights Academy, a dedicated digital learning platform designed to strengthen knowledge, practical skills, and confidence for human rights action. The Academy offers learning opportunities covering human rights principles, advocacy, protest, climate change, gender-based violence, energy transition, equality, justice, digital security, freedom of expression, and several other subjects connected with defending human dignity. The courses are online, self-guided, and free. Amnesty International’s current course page states that learning is available in more than 30 languages. Participants can begin with a short introductory lesson or explore the complete Academy catalogue for more detailed and specialized programmes. There is no fixed application deadline. Learners can register online, select an available course, and study according to their own schedule. Many courses award an official Amnesty International certificate after successful completion, although certificates are not available for every course. Participants should check the details of their selected course before enrolling if certification is important to them. The official programme information is available on the Amnesty International online courses page . Amnesty International Human Rights Academy overview Programme detail Information Learning provider Amnesty International Platform Amnesty Human Rights Academy Delivery format Online and self-guided Course fee Free Application deadline No fixed deadline Availability Rolling access throughout the year Languages More than 30 languages across the featured offering Course duration From short sessions to programmes lasting several hours Certificates Available for many courses, but not all Featured subjects Human rights, protest, climate change, gender-based violence and energy transition Registration Free online account Official registration Amnesty Human Rights Academy About Amnesty International’s Human Rights Academy The Human Rights Academy is Amnesty International’s online learning environment for human rights education. It was developed to make structured human rights learning accessible to people around the world and to strengthen the capacity of individuals to understand, claim, protect, and promote human rights. The Academy describes its approach as action-oriented education. This means the courses are not limited to presenting legal definitions or theoretical information. They are designed to help learners understand how human rights affect real people, communities, institutions, and public decisions. Participants are encouraged to connect their learning with practical and responsible action. Depending on the course, this may involve understanding a human rights problem, recognizing discrimination or abuse, communicating about rights, supporting affected communities, or developing more informed advocacy approaches. The platform contains both introductory and advanced material. This allows learners with limited previous knowledge to begin with basic concepts, while those with greater experience can explore more specialized subjects. Why human rights education is important Human rights affect almost every area of public and private life. They influence how governments exercise authority, how institutions treat individuals, how communities respond to inequality, and how people participate in social and political life. Human rights are connected to: Equality and non-discrimination Freedom of expression Freedom of peaceful assembly Access to justice Privacy and digital security Education Health Housing Food and water Environmental protection Gender equality Protection from violence Rights of refugees and migrants Civic participation Government accountability Despite their importance, many people encounter human rights terminology without receiving formal instruction on what those rights mean, how they are protected, or how violations can be addressed. Accessible human rights education can help learners: Understand foundational human rights principles Recognize the connection between dignity, equality, freedom, and justice Identify discrimination and other human rights concerns Understand the responsibilities of governments and institutions Examine contemporary social issues through a human rights perspective Communicate human rights issues more accurately Develop responsible advocacy and campaigning skills Build confidence to support constructive change Amnesty International’s Academy makes this learning available without requiring participants to attend a physical classroom or follow a fixed institutional timetable. Featured Amnesty International online courses Amnesty International’s official course page currently highlights five major learning opportunities of different lengths. Introduction to Human Rights Indicative duration: 1.5 hours The Introduction to Human Rights course provides a foundation for understanding what human rights are and why they matter. It can help learners become familiar with principles such as: Human dignity Equality Non-discrimination Freedom Justice Universality of human rights Responsibility and accountability This course can serve as a starting point before moving to more specialized Academy subjects. It may also help participants understand the wider context of Amnesty International’s research, campaigning, advocacy, and human rights education activities. The Right to Protest Indicative duration: 3 hours Peaceful protest is an important method through which individuals and communities express concerns, demand accountability, influence public debate, and advocate for social or political change. The Right to Protest course explores the relationship between protest and human rights, including the importance of peaceful assembly and freedom of expression. The subject is particularly relevant in environments where: Public demonstrations face restrictions Governments introduce protest-related legislation Law-enforcement responses raise human rights concerns Activists experience intimidation or harassment Digital surveillance affects civic participation Freedom of expression is under pressure The course can help learners understand why peaceful protest is protected and why restrictions on protest should be assessed carefully. Climate Change Indicative duration: 5 hours Climate change is not only an environmental issue. It can affect a wide range of internationally recognized rights, including rights connected with: Health Housing Food Water Livelihoods Equality Culture Development Life and personal security Climate change can also increase displacement, deepen existing inequalities, and place a disproportionate burden on communities that have contributed least to global emissions. This course gives learners an opportunity to examine climate change from a human rights perspective. It can help explain why environmental action should consider justice, participation, equality, accountability, and the needs of vulnerable communities. Gender-Based Violence Indicative duration: 1.5 hours Gender-based violence is a serious human rights concern that can occur in homes, schools, workplaces, communities, institutions, public spaces, and online environments. It can include physical, sexual, psychological, economic, and technology-facilitated forms of violence. Education is essential for: Understanding the causes of gender-based violence Identifying harmful gender norms and stereotypes Challenging discriminatory attitudes Supporting safer communities Promoting equality Improving awareness of available protections and support The course introduces issues connected with gender-based violence and helps learners examine the attitudes and structural conditions that allow such violence to continue. The Energy Transition Indicative duration: 45 minutes The global transition toward cleaner energy systems is essential for addressing climate change. However, energy decisions can also affect workers, local communities, Indigenous peoples, land, natural resources, and livelihoods. A transition that ignores human rights can create new inequalities or reproduce existing ones. This short course examines the relationship between changing energy systems and human rights. It can help learners understand why the transition should be environmentally sustainable, socially responsible, and fair to affected communities. Its 45-minute duration makes it suitable for people seeking a focused introduction to the subject. Additional subjects available through the Academy The featured courses represent only part of the Human Rights Academy catalogue. Additional learning may cover topics such as: Human rights advocacy and campaigning Freedom of expression Peaceful assembly Digital security Privacy and surveillance Human rights defenders Women’s rights Refugee and migrant rights Equality and non-discrimination Economic and social rights Justice and accountability Climate justice Community action Human rights education methods Protection of civic space Responsible campaigning Course availability may change as Amnesty International updates existing content, adds translations, and introduces new learning material. Learners should consult the live Academy catalogue for the most current course titles, durations, languages, and certificate arrangements. Free and self-paced learning The Academy follows a self-guided learning model. Participants can start a course and return to it when their schedule permits. This makes the platform useful for people balancing learning with employment, formal education, volunteering, family responsibilities, or community work. The format offers several practical advantages: No requirement to attend a scheduled physical class Flexibility to study at different times Ability to progress according to individual availability Access to short and longer learning formats Opportunity to revisit unfinished material Ability to choose subjects according to personal or professional interests Self-paced learning still requires discipline. Participants should establish a realistic study schedule instead of assuming that unlimited flexibility will automatically lead to completion. Course duration Course lengths vary considerably. Amnesty International’s broader human rights education page describes learning content ranging from approximately 15 minutes to 15 hours. The currently featured courses range from 45 minutes to five hours. Short courses may provide: A rapid introduction to a specific issue Essential definitions and principles Awareness of a current human rights concern A manageable starting point for new learners Longer courses may include: Detailed modules Case studies Graded exercises Coursework Assessments Action-planning activities Certificate requirements Before starting, learners should review the estimated duration and decide how the course will fit into their schedule. Languages and accessibility The official online-course page states that courses are available in more than 30 languages. Language availability varies by course. Not every course is necessarily available in every language. The Academy includes widely used languages such as: English Arabic French Spanish Russian Additional translations are available for different regions and communities. Learners should: Select their preferred platform language. Review the languages available for the chosen course. Confirm that the learning content and assessments are available in a language they can use confidently. Change the language in their profile later if they want to explore other course versions. Because the Academy is online, participants do not need to travel to a training venue. Actual accessibility will still depend on internet availability, device compatibility, language availability, and access to the Academy platform. Amnesty International certificates Many Human Rights Academy courses provide an official certificate, but not all courses do. Some short courses, including certain brief introductory programmes, may not offer certification. Learners should not assume that every Academy course automatically provides a certificate. Amnesty International explains that the Academy offers two principal types of certificates. Certificate of Participation A Certificate of Participation may be awarded after the successful completion of courses containing graded exercises or coursework. Certificate of Excellence A Certificate of Excellence may be awarded following successful completion of courses involving a more comprehensive assessment process. Certificate requirements vary by course. Before enrolling, learners should confirm: Whether the course offers a certificate Whether graded exercises are included Whether a minimum score is required Whether all modules must be completed Whether coursework must be submitted How the certificate is issued or downloaded Amnesty International’s certificate guidance is available through its Academy information page . A completion certificate should not be misrepresented as: A university degree A professional licence A formal academic qualification Guaranteed professional accreditation An employment guarantee A job offer from Amnesty International It documents successful completion of a specific Academy learning programme under that course’s conditions. Skills and knowledge participants may develop Learning outcomes depend on the selected course. Across the Academy, participants may strengthen knowledge and skills related to: Core human rights principles Human rights terminology Equality and non-discrimination Advocacy and campaigning Ethical communication Community engagement Gender equality Prevention of gender-based violence Freedom of expression Peaceful assembly Climate justice Environmental rights Digital rights and privacy Human rights analysis Responsible social action Understanding institutional obligations Translating knowledge into practical initiatives The courses can complement academic studies, professional development, teaching, training, civil-society work, volunteering, and community engagement. Their value will ultimately depend on whether participants understand the material and apply it responsibly in appropriate contexts. How to register Step 1: Visit the official course page Begin by opening: Amnesty International Free Online Courses This page presents the featured courses and provides access to the wider Academy platform. Step 2: Open the registration page Visit the official registration portal: Register for the Amnesty Human Rights Academy Step 3: Select a language Choose the preferred platform language. Amnesty states that learners can later change the language through their profile if they want to explore programmes offered in other languages. Step 4: Complete the registration form Provide the requested information, including: First name Last name Email address Password Other requested profile information The registered email address becomes the Academy username. Review the relevant privacy information before completing registration. Step 5: Activate the account The Academy will send an account-confirmation message to the registered email address. According to Amnesty International’s guidance, the confirmation link is valid for 48 hours. Check the inbox and, if necessary, the spam or junk folder for a message titled “Finish setting up your Amnesty Academy account.” Open the message and activate the account before the link expires. Step 6: Sign in Use the registered email address and password to access the Academy. Step 7: Browse the course catalogue Review the available courses and learning plans. Open the details page for any course of interest. Step 8: Check course conditions Before enrolling, confirm: Course content Estimated duration Available languages Assessment requirements Certificate availability Required completion score, where applicable Step 9: Start learning Work through the modules at a manageable pace and follow the course instructions. Step 10: Complete all requirements If the course offers a certificate, complete every required module, assessment, graded exercise, or coursework activity. How to make the most of the opportunity Establish a learning schedule Divide longer courses into manageable sessions and set a target completion date. Keep structured notes Record important concepts, legal principles, case studies, questions, and practical lessons. Connect learning with real issues Consider how the subject relates to policies, institutions, communities, and human rights challenges in your own context. Complete assessments carefully Read all instructions and verify that every required activity has been submitted. Check certificate conditions before starting Do not wait until the end to discover whether certification is available. Use the official platform The courses are free. Be cautious of third parties demanding payment for access to Amnesty International’s Academy content. Deadline and course availability There is no fixed application deadline for the general Human Rights Academy catalogue. Registration and course enrolment are available on a rolling basis throughout the year. Learners do not need to wait for a competitive admissions decision before beginning general Academy content. However, rolling access does not guarantee that every course will remain available permanently. Amnesty International may: Add new courses Update existing content Introduce additional languages Archive older material Change assessment requirements Modify certificate conditions Participants should therefore consult the live platform for current information. Important distinctions The Human Rights Academy is a free education platform. It is not a funded academic programme or employment scheme. It does not generally provide: University tuition funding A cash award A grant A paid placement An internship Employment Travel support Accommodation support Automatic professional accreditation Guaranteed employment with Amnesty International These distinctions are important when promoting the opportunity or listing a completed course on a CV, LinkedIn profile, or professional application. Official links Explore featured courses: Amnesty International Online Courses Register for the Academy: Amnesty Human Rights Academy Registration Browse the full catalogue: Amnesty Academy Learning Catalogue Learn about Amnesty’s human rights education work: Amnesty International Human Rights Education Conclusion Amnesty International’s Human Rights Academy provides an accessible way to study human rights through free, online, and self-paced courses. With learning available in more than 30 languages and content ranging from short introductory sessions to programmes lasting several hours, the Academy enables participants to select material suited to their interests, schedule, and existing knowledge. Featured courses cover important subjects such as an introduction to human rights, the right to protest, climate change, gender-based violence, and the energy transition. The broader Academy catalogue offers additional learning on advocacy, justice, equality, digital rights, freedom of expression, and other human rights issues. Many courses offer official Amnesty International certificates, but certification is course-specific. Participants should review the course-details page and complete all assessments or coursework required for their chosen programme. There is no fixed application deadline. Learners can register throughout the year through the official Amnesty Human Rights Academy platform. Anyone considering these courses should select a relevant subject, verify its language and certificate conditions, establish a realistic study schedule, and focus on applying the knowledge responsibly. Human rights education produces its greatest value when learning is transformed into informed, respectful, and constructive action. For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: Fully Funded PhD in Political Science at UCLouvain 2026 in Belgium: Study Inclusive Political Representation Through the WEAVE Research Project
summary: Political representation is one of the most debated and pressing issues in modern democracies. As societies become increasingly diverse, ensuring that all citizens—particularly those from marginalized and underrepresented communities—have a meaningful voice in democratic decision-making has become more important than ever. To address this challenge, UCLouvain (Université catholique de Louvain) in Belgium has announced applications for a fully funded PhD in Political Science under the prestigious WEAVE Project: Co-Designing Inclusive Political Representation . The doctoral position is funded by the FNRS and FWO , bringing together leading researchers from UCLouvain and Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) . This unique doctoral programme offers aspiring political scientists an exceptional opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research on democracy, political representation, participatory governance, and social inclusion while earning a joint doctoral degree from two internationally recognized Belgian universities. Applications are open until 31 August 2026 . About the PhD Programme The doctoral research position is hosted by the Political Sciences Institute within the Louvain-Europe Institute of the Social Sciences and Humanities sector at UCLouvain. The selected PhD researcher will become part of an ambitious European collaborative project exploring how democratic representation can be redesigned to better reflect the voices and experiences of people living in socio-economic precarity in Brussels. Unlike traditional political science projects that examine democratic systems from institutional or elite perspectives, this project adopts a bottom-up research approach , allowing individuals from structurally underrepresented communities to actively shape the research process. Participants will not simply serve as research subjects but will collaborate with researchers in: Identifying democratic challenges Sharing lived experiences Co-designing solutions Developing policy recommendations Reimagining political representation The project therefore combines rigorous academic scholarship with practical societal impact. About the WEAVE Project The PhD is part of the internationally funded research initiative: Co-Designing Inclusive Political Representation The project is jointly conducted by: UCLouvain Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) Funding is provided through: FNRS FWO The project examines questions such as: Who feels politically represented? Why do some citizens feel excluded from democratic systems? How can democratic institutions better include marginalized voices? What innovative forms of representation can strengthen democracy? How can communities participate in designing political reforms? The research combines several methodological approaches including: Democratic theory Participatory research Community-engaged scholarship Qualitative longitudinal research Co-design methodologies Policy-oriented research Researchers continuously move between empirical findings and theoretical reflection using an iterative abductive research design. What Makes This PhD Unique? This doctoral programme stands out because it combines academic excellence with real-world societal engagement. Instead of relying solely on traditional academic methods, the project actively involves community members in shaping the research itself. Successful candidates will: Work directly with communities in Brussels Collaborate with NGOs Engage with policy stakeholders Develop democratic reform proposals Produce academically rigorous research with practical relevance The programme also offers international collaboration through two major universities and exposure to leading experts in democratic theory and political science. Research Focus The successful doctoral candidate will conduct original research focusing on topics such as: Political representation Democratic participation Social inclusion Socio-economic precarity Participatory democracy Community-engaged governance Democratic innovation Inclusive policymaking Qualitative political research The candidate is expected to develop an original doctoral dissertation contributing new knowledge to political science while supporting the broader objectives of the WEAVE Project. Doctoral Supervision The PhD researcher will receive supervision from distinguished scholars including: Prof. Virginie Van Ingelgom Prof. Karen Celis Dr. Kenza Amara Hammou The supervisory team represents expertise across democratic theory, political participation, representation studies, and qualitative political research. Main Responsibilities Throughout the four-year programme, the doctoral researcher will undertake a wide range of academic and field-based responsibilities. These include: Developing an Original PhD Dissertation The successful applicant will design and conduct an independent research project that contributes original knowledge to political science. Conducting Participatory Fieldwork The project places strong emphasis on qualitative research. The doctoral researcher will: Conduct interviews Organize participatory workshops Facilitate panel discussions Lead co-design sessions Engage directly with research participants Fieldwork will primarily take place in Brussels. Collaborating with Community Organizations The researcher will establish partnerships with: Local NGOs Community organizations Civil society groups Local stakeholders These collaborations will ensure that research findings remain grounded in community experiences. Qualitative Data Analysis Responsibilities include: Coding interview data Thematic analysis Interpretation of qualitative findings Integrating empirical evidence into theoretical discussions Academic Publishing The doctoral candidate will contribute to: Journal articles Research reports Collaborative publications Conference papers Conference Participation Researchers will present findings at: National conferences International conferences Doctoral seminars Academic workshops This provides excellent opportunities to build international research networks. Public Engagement The project encourages researchers to communicate beyond academia. Activities include: Policy engagement Community dissemination Public presentations Stakeholder workshops Co-developed policy outputs Joint Doctoral Programme One of the strongest features of this opportunity is its joint institutional structure. The candidate will be enrolled in a collaborative doctoral programme between: UCLouvain Vrije Universiteit Brussel This arrangement offers: Joint doctoral degree Access to academic resources at both universities Dual supervision International networking Broader research opportunities Doctoral seminars at both institutions The programme structure includes: Years 1–2 Based at UCLouvain. Years 3–4 Based at Vrije Universiteit Brussel. Funding and Benefits The position includes comprehensive financial support. Benefits include: Fully funded four-year doctoral scholarship (48 months) Funding according to FNRS and FWO regulations Dedicated budget for qualitative fieldwork Conference participation funding Professional training support Research dissemination funding International academic networking opportunities Joint doctoral degree from two prestigious Belgian universities Supervision by leading political science scholars Access to seminars and doctoral training at both institutions Opportunity to collaborate with NGOs and policymakers Participation in a major European research collaboration Eligibility Requirements Applicants should possess the following qualifications. Academic Background Applicants should have: A Master s degree in Political Science or A Master s degree in a related social science discipline. Final-year Master s students are also encouraged to apply. Research Interests Applicants should demonstrate strong interest in: Political representation Democracy Qualitative research Participatory research Community-engaged research Language Requirements Applicants must possess: Excellent spoken French Excellent written English Excellent spoken English Knowledge of Dutch is considered an advantage but is not mandatory. Additional Skills Successful candidates should demonstrate: Intellectual curiosity Initiative Independent working ability Teamwork skills Willingness to conduct extensive qualitative fieldwork in Brussels Required Application Documents Applicants should combine documents into a single PDF whenever possible. The application package should include: Cover letter (maximum two pages) Curriculum Vitae (CV) Statement of research interests and project ideas (maximum one page) Master s thesis or another writing sample Academic diploma Contact information for two academic referees Recommendation letters are not required at the application stage. Important Application Instructions Applicants should note the following requirements carefully: Use the email subject line: PhD Position (4 years) in Political Science Co-Designing Inclusive Political Representation Applications submitted without the required subject line may not be considered. Late applications will not be accepted. Recruitment Timeline Applicants should take note of the following schedule: Application Deadline: 31 August 2026 Shortlisted candidates informed: Early September 2026 Interviews: Second half of September 2026 Starting date: 1 October 2026 APPLY HERE Why You Should Apply This PhD offers considerably more than a traditional doctoral programme. It allows researchers to: Work on a highly relevant democratic issue Influence public policy Engage directly with communities Conduct innovative participatory research Gain international academic experience Build collaborations across universities Receive generous doctoral funding Publish internationally Develop expertise valued in academia, policy institutions, NGOs, and international organizations For anyone passionate about democracy, political participation, and social justice, this programme provides an exceptional platform to build an impactful academic career. Visit HERE to learn more about the Fully Funded PhD in Political Science at UCLouvain 2026 in Belgium Conclusion The UCLouvain PhD in Political Science under the WEAVE Project represents a rare opportunity to contribute to transformative research on democratic inclusion and political representation while studying within an internationally collaborative environment. Through generous funding, expert supervision, joint training at UCLouvain and Vrije Universiteit Brussel, and extensive engagement with communities, policymakers, and civil society organizations, doctoral researchers will gain the academic and practical skills needed to become future leaders in political science. If you are motivated by research that combines theoretical excellence with real-world impact, this fully funded doctoral opportunity is well worth considering. Be sure to prepare a strong application and submit it before the 31 August 2026 deadline. title: FAO Fellows Programme 2026: Global Research Assignments at FAO Offices Worldwide
summary: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations has opened applications for its 2026 Call for Expression of Interest for the Fellows Programme. The call covers FAO headquarters, regional and subregional offices, country offices, and liaison offices in various locations worldwide. Through this programme, FAO seeks individuals with advanced technical knowledge, professional experience, and research expertise who can pursue specialized learning objectives while contributing meaningfully to the Organization’s work. Assignments may last for up to 11 months and will be matched to the candidate’s expertise and the operational needs of the hosting FAO office. All assignments are expected to support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, FAO’s Strategic Framework, and the transformation of agrifood systems. Applications must be submitted through the official FAO recruitment portal by 25 August 2026 . A crucial condition must be understood before applying: FAO does not pay fellows a salary, stipend, or other remuneration. Candidates must be fully sponsored by an external entity and must identify their sponsoring institution in the application. FAO Fellows Programme 2026 overview Programme detail Official information Organization Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Vacancy announcement 2600010 Posting date 25 January 2026 Application deadline 25 August 2026 Organizational coverage FAO headquarters, regional, subregional, country, and liaison offices Location Various locations Maximum duration Up to 11 months Grade level Not applicable Post number Not applicable CCOG code Not applicable FAO remuneration None External sponsorship Mandatory Application method Online through the official FAO recruitment portal Required attachments Research proposal and evidence of recognized academic attendance or qualifications About the Food and Agriculture Organization FAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to eliminate hunger, improve food security and nutrition, and ensure that people have regular access to sufficient and high-quality food. The Organization has 195 Members and operates in more than 130 countries. Its work brings together governments, researchers, technical experts, development institutions, communities, and other partners to address complex global and national challenges affecting agriculture and food systems. Although FAO is commonly associated with agricultural production, its work covers a much broader range of areas, including: Food security and nutrition Sustainable agriculture Agrifood-system transformation Rural development Agricultural economics and markets Climate-change adaptation and mitigation Fisheries and aquaculture Forestry and biodiversity Livestock and animal health Natural-resource management Food safety and international standards Agricultural data and statistics Social protection and rural livelihoods Emergency response and resilience Institutional governance and capacity development Innovation, technology and digital agriculture Monitoring, evaluation and impact assessment The programme can therefore accommodate expertise from several academic and professional disciplines, provided the proposed work has a clear connection with FAO’s mandate. Purpose of the FAO Fellows Programme The Fellows Programme aims to connect advanced academic and research expertise with FAO’s practical technical, policy and development work. It typically attracts people who already possess considerable knowledge and experience in a field relevant to FAO. These individuals are expected to pursue clearly defined learning or research objectives while contributing their technical expertise to the hosting office. The arrangement is intended to provide value to both parties: The fellow gains exposure to FAO’s international technical and policy environment. FAO receives specialized research, analysis, knowledge or technical support. The hosting office can benefit from contemporary academic methods and evidence. The fellow can connect academic or professional expertise with real institutional and development challenges. This is not intended to be a passive study visit. Each assignment is a structured and time-bound arrangement based on the requirements of an FAO office and the expertise of the selected fellow. Alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals Every assignment should align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and FAO’s Strategic Framework. FAO’s transformation agenda focuses on creating agrifood systems that are: More efficient More inclusive More resilient More sustainable The Organization expresses this vision through its Four Betters: Better production Better nutrition A better environment A better life These priorities support FAO’s contribution to the 2030 Agenda and its commitment to leaving no one behind. Applicants should therefore connect their proposed research or technical work with a specific development challenge. A proposal will be stronger when it explains how the expected findings or outputs can support FAO programmes, policies, Member Nations or relevant SDG targets. Potential technical areas of assignment The announcement does not restrict fellows to one discipline. The specific field of work will depend on the applicant’s profile and the needs of the Organization. Potential areas may include: Hunger reduction and food security Nutrition and healthy diets Sustainable agricultural production Climate-resilient agriculture Agricultural value chains and markets Rural development and livelihoods Food-loss and food-waste reduction Natural-resource and ecosystem management Water and soil management Forestry, fisheries and aquaculture Livestock development and animal health Agricultural trade and economics Food safety and quality standards Social protection and inclusive rural development Women’s economic participation in agrifood systems Youth engagement and employment Agricultural statistics and data systems Monitoring and evaluation Policy research and impact assessment Digital agriculture and technological innovation Disaster-risk reduction and emergency response Institutional governance and capacity development Knowledge management and partnerships This list is illustrative rather than exhaustive. FAO will determine the actual technical focus according to organizational priorities and the needs of the relevant hosting office. Reporting arrangements Each selected fellow will report to an assigned supervisor. The responsible FAO office will prepare specific Terms of Reference before the assignment begins. These Terms of Reference will define: The purpose of the assignment The fellow’s duties and responsibilities Research or learning objectives Required technical contributions Expected deliverables Reporting arrangements Assignment duration Relevant deadlines and milestones Supervision and coordination arrangements Because each Terms of Reference is developed by the hiring office, the duties will differ between assignments. A fellow may undertake research, policy analysis, data analysis, evidence synthesis, programme support, technical documentation, knowledge-sharing activities or methodological development. Applicants should not assume that all FAO offices offer identical assignments. Selection depends on whether a particular office has a genuine need that matches the applicant’s background. Assignment locations The call covers: FAO headquarters Regional offices Subregional offices Country offices Liaison offices The official location is stated as “Various Locations.” Fellows can be assigned to an FAO office where a suitable technical match and hosting arrangement exist. A candidate does not automatically receive the right to select any FAO office or country. The final location will depend on: Organizational requirements Availability of a suitable hosting office Technical compatibility Agreement between the fellow and hosting office Sponsorship arrangements Immigration and residence requirements Selected candidates must have appropriate residence or immigration status in the proposed country of assignment before joining the Organization. Applicants should not assume that FAO will automatically secure immigration permission on their behalf. Duration of the assignment An assignment can last for up to a maximum of 11 months. The actual duration may be shorter depending on: The approved Terms of Reference Research and learning objectives Hosting-office requirements Availability of external sponsorship Agreed deliverables and work plan Operational or immigration considerations Applicants should develop a research plan that can reasonably be completed within the proposed assignment period. Financial and sponsorship conditions FAO does not provide remuneration to fellows. This means the programme does not offer: A salary A monthly stipend Standard employee compensation FAO-funded accommodation Candidates must be fully sponsored by an external entity. The name of the sponsoring institution or institutions should be mentioned in the application. Applicants should clarify the exact financial coverage with their proposed sponsor before applying. Depending on the sponsorship agreement, matters requiring confirmation may include: Travel expenses Accommodation Living costs Local transportation Visa-related expenses Research costs Medical insurance Other assignment-related expenses Applicants should not wait until selection to begin looking for sponsorship. A credible and confirmed sponsorship arrangement is a central programme condition. Medical coverage and insurance FAO provides medical coverage for service-incurred matters and pays the related premium. However, fellows must arrange and pay for medical insurance covering non-service-incurred matters throughout their assignment. Applicants should therefore review their insurance position carefully and confirm that they will have suitable medical coverage for the entire assignment period. Accommodation arrangements FAO does not provide financial or organizational assistance for accommodation. The fellow, or the sponsoring institution where applicable, is responsible for arranging and funding accommodation at the duty station. Candidates should research living costs and accommodation availability before accepting any proposed assignment. FAO core competencies Candidates will be assessed against the following core competencies: Results Focus Teamwork Communication Building Effective Relationships Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement Applicants should demonstrate these competencies through concrete professional, academic or research examples rather than simply listing them. For example, candidates can describe situations in which they: Delivered measurable research or programme results Worked successfully with multidisciplinary teams Communicated technical information to non-technical audiences Built relationships with institutions or stakeholders Shared knowledge or introduced improved working methods FAO professional values All candidates are expected to uphold FAO’s principal values: Commitment to FAO Respect for All Integrity and Transparency FAO is committed to workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture. The Organization maintains zero tolerance for: Sexual exploitation and abuse Sexual harassment Abuse of authority Discrimination Conduct inconsistent with FAO’s mandate or United Nations standards Selected candidates will undergo reference and background checks. Applications will be handled with strict confidentiality. FAO is also a non-smoking work environment. Documents required for the application Applicants must complete an online profile through the FAO recruitment portal. The profile should accurately include: Complete employment history Research experience Academic qualifications Language proficiency Technical knowledge Relevant skills Other information requested by the recruitment system Candidates must also attach: A research proposal Evidence of attendance at a recognized university or copies of relevant academic qualifications FAO screens applications using the information entered in the online profile. Applicants should not assume that uploading a CV or proposal will compensate for an incomplete profile. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Preparing a strong research proposal FAO requires applicants to attach a research proposal, although the public vacancy announcement does not specify a universal format or word limit. Unless additional instructions appear in the recruitment portal, a strong proposal should cover: 1. Research title Use a focused and technically relevant title that clearly identifies the proposed subject. 2. Background and problem statement Explain the policy, technical, institutional or development problem that the research will address. 3. Relevance to FAO Describe how the proposed work connects with FAO’s mandate, Strategic Framework and areas of technical responsibility. 4. SDG alignment Identify the Sustainable Development Goals and targets to which the proposed work can contribute. 5. Research objectives State clear, measurable and realistic objectives. 6. Methodology Explain the methods, data sources, analytical framework, research tools or consultation processes that will be used. 7. Expected outputs Possible outputs might include: A research paper Policy recommendations A technical report A data-analysis framework A methodology or toolkit A knowledge product A monitoring framework A capacity-development resource Applicants should not promise a particular output unless it is feasible within the proposed duration. 8. Practical contribution Explain how the work could support FAO, a hosting office, Member Nations or relevant agrifood-system stakeholders. 9. Work plan Provide a realistic sequence of activities, milestones and expected completion dates. 10. Applicant’s contribution Explain the knowledge, professional experience and technical capabilities that distinguish the applicant. 11. Ethical and data considerations Address research ethics, confidentiality, data protection, stakeholder consent or other relevant safeguards. This structure is practical guidance rather than a prescribed FAO template. Applicants should follow any additional instructions shown in the official recruitment portal. How to apply Step 1: Open the official vacancy Visit the FAO vacancy announcement 2600010 . Step 2: Create or access your candidate account First-time applicants must create an online candidate profile. Existing applicants should log in and review their information. Step 3: Complete the entire profile Provide accurate information about: Employment Research Education Languages Technical expertise Relevant experience Step 4: Confirm external sponsorship Identify a credible sponsoring institution and discuss the proposed financial arrangements. Do not name an institution as a confirmed sponsor unless it has genuinely agreed to support the assignment. Step 5: Prepare the research proposal Tailor the proposal to FAO’s mandate, Strategic Framework and relevant Sustainable Development Goals. Step 6: Upload supporting documents Attach the research proposal and the required evidence of academic attendance or qualifications. Check that every document: Opens correctly Is clearly readable Has the correct filename Has been uploaded in the appropriate section Contains current and accurate information Step 7: Apply specifically to announcement 2600010 Creating a candidate profile does not constitute an application. The candidate must open the specific vacancy and formally submit the application. Step 8: Confirm submission Check the portal to ensure the application status shows that it has been submitted successfully. Step 9: Apply before the final day FAO encourages candidates to submit well before the deadline. Early submission provides time to resolve technical, login or document-upload problems. Only applications received through the official FAO recruitment portal will be considered. Screening and selection process Applications will be reviewed according to the information provided in the online profile and attachments. Only qualified candidates selected for an interview will be contacted directly by the responsible hiring office. Submitting an application does not guarantee: An interview Selection A placement Assignment to a preferred location Future consideration under another call FAO does not maintain a continuing roster of unsuccessful Fellows Programme applicants. Candidates who are not selected before the closing date and want to remain under consideration must apply again when a new Call for Expression of Interest is published. Personal-data processing Information submitted through the recruitment portal may be shared within FAO and with organizations acting on FAO’s behalf to provide recruitment-support services. These services may include: Application pre-screening Assessments Background checks Reference verification Related recruitment support Applicants will be asked to provide consent before submitting their application. A candidate may withdraw consent by withdrawing the application. However, FAO will then be unable to continue considering that application. Application deadline The application deadline is 25 August 2026 . FAO explains that the closing date and time displayed on the vacancy page may reflect the date and time settings of the applicant’s device. Its general application guidance states that vacancy announcements are removed from the career site at 23:59 Central European Time on the closing date. Applicants should consult the live vacancy page for the localized closing time and submit several days early. Common mistakes applicants should avoid Assuming that FAO provides a salary or stipend Applying without a credible external sponsor Naming an organization as a sponsor without securing its agreement Submitting a generic research proposal Failing to connect the proposal with FAO’s mandate Leaving profile sections incomplete Providing inconsistent dates or employment details Uploading unreadable or incorrect documents Omitting evidence of academic qualifications Creating a profile without formally submitting the application Attempting to submit an application by email Waiting until the final hours Miscalculating the deadline because of time-zone differences Recruitment safeguards FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of its recruitment process, including: Application Interview Processing Selection Training Applicants should reject any request for payment claiming to be connected to FAO recruitment. Applications must be submitted through the official career portal. FAO support or Fellows Programme email addresses may respond to appropriate questions, but they do not accept applications. Official application link Applications should be submitted through the official FAO recruitment portal: Apply for the FAO Fellows Programme 2026 Applicants may also consult: Official FAO Fellows Programme page FAO Fellows Programme FAQs FAO application guidance Conclusion The FAO Fellows Programme 2026 provides an important opportunity for advanced researchers and technical specialists to connect their expertise with the work of a major United Nations organization. Selected fellows may contribute to research, evidence, policies, programmes, data systems and technical solutions supporting food security, sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, better nutrition and inclusive agrifood-system transformation. Nevertheless, applicants must assess the conditions realistically. The programme does not provide a salary or stipend, requires full external sponsorship, does not fund or arrange accommodation, and requires fellows to obtain their own non-service medical insurance. A competitive application will require more than strong academic qualifications. Candidates should present a focused research proposal, demonstrate relevant experience, connect their work with FAO priorities and the SDGs, submit complete documentation, and establish a credible sponsorship arrangement. The deadline is 25 August 2026 . Eligible candidates should apply early through the official FAO recruitment portal. For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: UpTide Accelerator 2026: Receive a $5,000 Grant, Up to $25,000 in Additional Funding, and Expert Support to Scale Your U.S. Nonprofit
summary: Nonprofit organizations play a vital role in addressing some of society’s most pressing challenges. Rather than supporting organizations that are still testing ideas, the accelerator focuses on nonprofits that have already developed scalable and replicable models capable of strengthening communities and increasing social connection. The program recognizes that many of today s societal challenges stem from increasing isolation and declining community engagement. Through funding, mentorship, and organizational development, UpTide helps nonprofit leaders strengthen their organizations so they can reach even more people. The accelerator combines strategic planning, leadership development, coaching, networking, and funding into one comprehensive experience. Program Benefits Selected organizations gain access to a wide range of financial and professional development opportunities designed to support sustainable organizational growth. Participants will receive: A $5,000 unrestricted grant upon successfully completing every component of the accelerator. A fully funded New York City residency week , including flights, hotel accommodation, and most meals. The opportunity to compete for up to $25,000 in additional grant funding by presenting their organization during Showcase Day. New York City Leadership Week Participants will travel to New York City for an immersive week of programming focused on nonprofit leadership and organizational growth. This roadmap helps nonprofit leaders: Scale their programs sustainably. Strengthen operational capacity. Expand partnerships. Increase long-term impact. Focus on addressing community disconnection and strengthening community relationships. Operate programs that directly contribute to building stronger communities. Program Impact Requirements Organizations should demonstrate measurable impact by: Directly serving at least 500 people , or Serving a significant proportion of their target community. Applicants must also have: At least one proven intervention. A minimum of one year of positive impact data demonstrating successful outcomes. Scalability Requirements The accelerator seeks nonprofits that have already demonstrated success and are prepared for expansion. Organizations should have: A proven and replicable model. Evidence of meaningful community impact. Strong potential for scaling to serve additional communities. Time Commitment Participants are expected to fully engage in every component of the accelerator. To qualify for the unrestricted grant, organizations must attend: All virtual sessions. New York City Week. Showcase Day. Failure to complete all required activities may affect eligibility for the grant. The Center is recognized for creating major global initiatives including: GivingTuesday Social Good Summit Share Our America The Center also brings significant experience in managing leadership fellowship programs. Over the past decade, SEED SPOT has: Supported more than 4,000 entrepreneurs. Helped create nearly 10,000 jobs. Focused on empowering underrepresented entrepreneurs across multiple sectors. Its expertise in accelerator programming strengthens the UpTide experience for nonprofit leaders. Why You Should Apply The UpTide Accelerator offers much more than grant funding. title: UNITAR Digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme 2026 for Ukrainian Women Refugees and Internally Displaced Women in Ukraine | Fully Funded AI, GIS and Python Training

title: Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships 2027 in Australia: Receive Up to AUD 180,000 to Scale Innovative Social and Environmental Solution
summary: The 2027 Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships are now accepting Expressions of Interest from exceptional Australian innovators who are developing transformative solutions to some of Australia s most urgent social and environmental challenges. Established by the Sidney Myer Fund and The Myer Foundation , the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships provide outstanding individuals with the time, financial support, expert guidance, mentorship, and professional network needed to significantly expand the impact of their innovative initiatives. Unlike many funding opportunities that focus on delivering predetermined outputs or strict performance indicators, this Fellowship is designed to give talented innovators the freedom to dedicate twelve months exclusively to advancing existing high-impact projects that demonstrate strong potential for lasting societal and environmental change. Each selected Fellow receives funding of up to AUD 180,000 over a twelve-month period, allowing them to step away from their regular employment and fully concentrate on developing innovative solutions capable of creating meaningful and scalable impact across Australia. About the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships The Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships were established to encourage bold thinking, innovative leadership, and entrepreneurial approaches to addressing complex societal issues. The Fellowship recognizes that many groundbreaking ideas require dedicated time, financial security, mentorship, and strategic support before they can reach their full potential. Rather than funding organizations, the Fellowship invests directly in individuals whose ideas have already demonstrated traction and are ready to move to the next stage of development. Successful Fellows become part of a growing network of innovators who are committed to creating sustainable, long-term solutions that benefit Australian communities. Fellowship Themes Applicants must propose projects aligned with one or more of the following priority themes: Inclusion Equality Sustainability Environment, including Climate Change Human, Civil Legal Rights Projects should clearly demonstrate how they contribute to solving major challenges within these focus areas. Fellowship Benefits Each successful Fellow may receive funding worth up to AUD 180,000 , including: 1. Personal Fellowship Stipend Recipients receive: AUD 140,000 stipend Financial support throughout the twelve-month Fellowship Opportunity to dedicate full-time attention to their project 2. Project Funding An additional up to AUD 40,000 is available for approved project-related expenses, including: Renting dedicated workspace Professional travel Hiring external consultants or specialists Other approved Fellowship-related costs Project expenses are reimbursed based on approved expenditure. 3. Professional Development Support Beyond funding, Fellows gain access to: Quarterly meetings with a panel of experienced experts One-on-one mentorship Networking opportunities with previous Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellows Guidance from Fellowship staff and advisors Access to an influential innovation community Who Should Apply? The Fellowship welcomes individuals from diverse professional backgrounds, sectors, and lived experiences. Applicants are encouraged to submit an Expression of Interest if they are leading innovative projects capable of delivering significant social or environmental impact. Ideal Projects Projects should be: High-impact Innovative or uniquely applied Capable of generating measurable outcomes Scalable Sustainable over time Focused on addressing significant Australian challenges Innovation may involve creating entirely new approaches or adapting proven ideas to new contexts. Ideal Applicants Strong applicants typically demonstrate: Significant experience in their field Entrepreneurial thinking A proven record of achievement Passion for their cause Strong professional networks Curiosity and willingness to learn Ability to collaborate effectively Commitment to making the most of the Fellowship experience Eligibility Requirements To qualify, applicants must: Be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. Reside in Australia for most of the Fellowship period. Be willing to take a twelve-month sabbatical from their current role. Demonstrate a strong history of achievement. Show entrepreneurial and innovative thinking. Be capable of transforming ideas into practical action. Have established networks related to their project. Project Eligibility Requirements Eligible projects must: Be based in Australia. Align with one or more Fellowship themes. Have been in development for no longer than three years . What Fellows Are Expected to Do The Fellowship is intentionally flexible. Rather than requiring recipients to meet rigid performance targets, Fellows are encouraged to use the year to advance their initiatives thoughtfully and strategically. During the Fellowship, recipients are expected to: Focus full-time on their project. Participate in Fellowship activities. Engage with mentors and advisors. Present a mid-term progress update. Deliver a final presentation at the conclusion of the Fellowship. Funding Exclusions The Fellowship does not support: Projects older than three years. Academic research projects. Higher degree coursework or dissertations. Medical research. Disease-specific initiatives. International projects. Scholarships. Sponsorships. Funding hubs or accelerator programs. Creative arts projects. Collaborative applications involving multiple individuals. Organizational applications. Capital campaigns. Endowment campaigns. Fundraising events. Program or service delivery projects without innovation potential. Curriculum or education development projects for schools, universities, or educational institutions. Application Process The Fellowship follows a multi-stage selection process designed to identify Australia s most promising innovators. Stage 1: Expression of Interest Applicants submit an online Expression of Interest (EOI) during the application window. Stage 2: Initial Review Following the closing date, applications undergo an extensive assessment process. Stage 3: Shortlisting Selected applicants are invited to prepare a detailed application. Stage 4: Interviews Shortlisted candidates participate in interviews. Stage 5: Final Selection Successful Fellows are confirmed following completion of the interview process. 2027 Application Timeline Applicants should carefully note the official timeline: 13 July 2026 – Expressions of Interest open. 16 August 2026 (11:59 PM AEST) – Expressions of Interest close. Week beginning 19 October 2026 – Shortlisted candidates invited to submit detailed applications. 10 January 2027 (11:59 PM AEDT) – Detailed applications due. February 2027 – Interviews conducted. March 2027 – Successful Fellows announced. Late submissions will not be accepted under any circumstances, including technical difficulties or personal issues. Applicants are also not permitted to submit additional materials after the application deadline. These examples demonstrate the Fellowship s commitment to supporting innovative ideas with the potential to create nationwide impact. Why Apply? The Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships represent one of Australia s premier opportunities for innovators seeking the resources and freedom to expand transformative ideas. Recipients receive generous financial support, mentorship, professional guidance, expert advice, and access to an influential community of previous Fellows, enabling them to focus entirely on scaling initiatives that can improve lives and strengthen Australian society. If you have an innovative project addressing inclusion, environmental sustainability, climate action, or human rights, this Fellowship provides a unique platform to accelerate your work and maximize long-term impact. Conclusion The 2027 Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships offer a rare opportunity for Australia s most innovative changemakers to dedicate an entire year to advancing bold ideas capable of solving significant social and environmental challenges. With funding of up to AUD 180,000 , extensive mentoring, strategic guidance, and access to a powerful network of innovators, the Fellowship is designed to help individuals transform promising initiatives into sustainable, scalable solutions that deliver lasting benefits across Australia. Eligible innovators are encouraged to carefully review the eligibility criteria and submit their Expression of Interest before the application deadline of 16 August 2026 .
